partners.diseaseBName: autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia due to CSF3R deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: CSF3R (HGNC:2439) —INCREASES→ JAK/STAT signaling pathway activation (REACT:R-HSA-181733); JAK/STAT signaling pathway activation (REACT:R-HSA-181733) —LEADS_TO→ Neutrophilia (HP:0011213); CSF3R (HGNC:2439) —DISRUPTS→ Granulopoiesis (GO:0000746); Granulopoiesis (GO:0000746) —LEADS_TO→ Severe congenital neutropenia (HP:0001891). Activating mutations in CSF3R lead to constitutive activation of the JAK/STAT signaling pathway, resulting in neutrophilia (Disease A). Conversely, loss-of-function mutations in CSF3R disrupt normal granulopoiesis, leading to severe congenital neutropenia (Disease B). Both disease mechanisms converge on the CSF3R gene and its role in granulopoiesis, albeit with opposite functional consequences.

raw.translational: Understanding the opposing functional consequences of CSF3R mutations in these two conditions could inform targeted therapeutic strategies. For gain-of-function mutations leading to neutrophilia, inhibitors of the JAK/STAT pathway might be considered. #### 1. autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia due to CSF3R deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.500)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-449836, Reactome:R-HSA-9616222, Reactome:R-HSA-9674555, Reactome:R-HSA-9705462)

**Proposed mechanism:** CSF3R (HGNC:2439) —INCREASES→ JAK/STAT signaling pathway activation (REACT:R-HSA-181733); JAK/STAT signaling pathway activation (REACT:R-HSA-181733) —LEADS_TO→ Neutrophilia (HP:0011213); CSF3R (HGNC:2439) —DISRUPTS→ Granulopoiesis (GO:0000746); Granulopoiesis (GO:0000746) —LEADS_TO→ Severe congenital neutropenia (HP:0001891). Activating mutations in CSF3R lead to constitutive activation of the JAK/STAT signaling pathway, resulting in neutrophilia (Disease A). Conversely, loss-of-function mutations in CSF3R disrupt normal granulopoiesis, leading to severe congenital neutropenia (Disease B). Both disease mechanisms converge on the CSF3R gene and its role in granulopoiesis, albeit with opposite functional consequences.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in CSF3R with a loss-of-function effect in patients diagnosed with hereditary neutrophilia, or a gain-of-function effect in patients with autosomal recessive severe congenital neutropenia. _(variant: rs75618545)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the opposing functional consequences of CSF3R mutations in these two conditions could inform targeted therapeutic strategies. For gain-of-function mutations leading to neutrophilia, inhibitors of the JAK/STAT pathway might be considered. For loss-of-function mutations causing neutropenia, therapies aimed at boosting granulopoiesis, such as G-CSF (granulocyte colony-stimulating factor), are already in use and could be further optimized.
